held_dispositions.disposition: FDOT general rest-area PDF is a historical copy ending with 2007 amendment history. Current FDOT Q&A supports 3-hour general / 10-hour HOS-commercial context, but no unconditional duration. Only separate Turnpike prohibition is projected.
10/16 consecutive-hour split needs route/facility predicates; only camping prohibition projected.
Both official JCAR URLs returned HTTP 503 in the independent attempt. Earlier claimed confirmations do not supply current raw proof. No reclassification.

2022 official compilation confirms historical text, not current edition. Official current-publications index could not be read (403). Original excerpt-verification timestamp is in the future. No positive camping grant projected.

Current official page verifies four hours in any 24 per person/group, with permit/work exceptions and excluded commercial service areas. 2026-03-20 is certification history, not a new amendment date. Hold numeric mapping until interval/exemption predicates exist.

All four official pages re-fetched via redirect to regs.maryland.gov and quoted rules confirmed. Overnight parking/camping prohibitions apply to SHA public-use-area scope, not an assumed MDTA plaza class. Page requests no scraping and offers bulk downloads; it carries CC BY-NC-SA / later CC0 notice. Hold automated retrieval/raw redistribution route for review; retain verified facts and paraphrases separately.

2026 statutory page confirms the HOS-commercial/operator/suitable-stall conditions. Agency page supports four hours for other motorists only where posted. All three activity fields remain unknown. Hold unconditional numeric mapping; 2008 is history, not the current edition.
Published 10-hour context is advisory NDOT guidance, not a standalone parking statute. Camping has statutory designated-site exceptions. Only conservative activity facts projected.

Cited administrative text prohibits erecting tents/booths/structures for camping or other activities. It does not establish an unrestricted camping prohibition for a parked RV. Correct broad camping value to unknown; retain the structure-specific restriction as text. Highway abandoned-vehicle provision is not a stay-permission or parking-duration grant.

Only ODOT camping prohibition projected. Unattended-vehicle three-hour rule is not a general stay cap. Turnpike positive grant is limited to RVs/travel trailers in designated lots at eight named plazas, one night, with payment, capacity and length conditions. Requires explicit vehicle/facility eligibility model before any positive grant.

Current TripCheck operating rules confirm camping prohibition and 12-in-24 context. Original 2019 legal-history entry is temporary and expired in 2020; do not call it an unqualified current effective date. Keep current page/date and separate statute-history provenance.
Official TDOT URL returned HTTP 503 in independent retrieval. No raw-response proof; earlier claimed verification not promoted.

Current UDOT page prohibits overnight camping, not unqualified all camping, and separately describes monitored extended stays. Broader camping remains unknown; preserve overnight-camping restriction as qualified text.
Explicit current prohibitions independently verified. Vehicle-sleeping status stays unknown; building-only sleeping ban is not extended to vehicles.
Activity fact independently verified. Eight-hour duration cannot be unconditional because authorization, posted, HOS-commercial and disabled-vehicle provisions differ.
